reviews.text: My dog, Bella was diagnosed with a possible heart murmur and she was referred to the wonderful cardiologist specialist, Dr. Tom Mullany at Nutgrove Veterinary Hospital. Tom took the time to perform an ECG and Cardiology Ultrasound and he explained the step by step procedure, the findings and potential issues in great detail. There was no doubt, Bella was in good hands with the knowledge, care and professionalism provided by Tom.The clinic was also exceptionally clean. The front desk nurses were also lovely to deal with despite it being so busy - we know why! Five stars, highly recommend.

I honestly can’t thank the wonderful team at Nutgrove Vets enough for the care and kindness they have shown my dog since he was very young. When he became seriously ill, it was an incredibly worrying time for us, but thanks to their diligence, patience and thorough diagnosis, he was given the treatment and care he needed and was nursed back to full health.

A huge and heartfelt thank you to Dr. William Hayden for his expertise, dedication and genuine care throughout. I’ll always be grateful for everything he did for our dog.

And a very special shout-out to Amber, whose warmth and kindness always made our visits so much easier — and even enjoyable for my dog!

It means so much to know your pet is in the hands of people who genuinely care. We will always be incredibly grateful to everyone at Nutgrove Vets and couldn’t recommend them highly enough.
Fantastic and friendly service from Nutgrove Vets, and the new building is great.

Funny in the front cover of this they have a picture of my dog rocky who is now dead when we brought him in they charged us 160 for a shot and wanted 400 euro which we didn’t have at the time so they sent us home after we told them he was poisoned rocky died that night. He is the dog with the bandana around his neck

Highly professional and honest cardiology specialists! I brought my Maine Coon here for a heart murmur. Dr Tom was incredibly thorough with the echocardiogram and ECG, explaining everything clearly and professionally.  Every single penny was spent transparently and was absolutely worth it for the peace of mind. Highly recommend their cardiology team thanks a lot Dr Tom and Sarah. See u in 2-3 years.

This is my experience in Nutgrove Veterinary Hospital — and why I will never return.

My dog had surgery at Nutgrove in February 2026 to remove a cancerous growth from his leg. The tumour was successfully removed and for that I am grateful.

However, within 30 minutes of leaving the practice, my dog's wound was bleeding badly. When I inspected it, there were no external sutures — the lips of the wound were not connected and blood was oozing from the incision. I photographed it and contacted the vet immediately. I was told the wound had been closed with glue. I couldn’t understand why glue rather than stitches were used, as the wound is large and located on his leg — a highly mobile part of his body. Within hours, the wound was completely open. For the benefit of people who are squeamish, I will not share the photos here.

My dog spent 9 weeks rather than 10 days in a cone, in constant discomfort. I had to clean his wound twice a day from mid-February until it eventually closed in May.

Considering everything that my dog went through and the workload that was created by this, when my dog eventually healed, I asked to be refunded the cost of the surgery, €705. When I raised the matter of the fee, the practice offered a partial refund of half the amount — on the condition that I sign a release note waiving any further recourse. On principle, I declined.

For me, my family and especially my elderly dog, this has been a nightmarish experience, and one I lay firmly at the door of the Nutgrove Veterinary Hospital, which is why I will never return. Obviously, you can make your own decisions about what is best for your dog but I felt it was important to share my experience.

For the past 7 years, Darragh has looked after my best pal, Charlie, with incredible care, patience, and compassion. He always took the time to find sensible solutions for every ailment and made sure Charlie was comfortable and well cared for throughout her life.

Charlie recently passed away, and I miss her dearly, but I wanted to thank Darragh for everything he did for her — especially in her final weeks. His kindness and support helped make that time as comfortable and peaceful as possible, and allowed us to truly cherish our last weeks together.

I’ll always be grateful for the care he gave to Charlie, and I couldn’t recommend him highly enough.

William was absolutely fantastic, he is an expert at what he does and you can feel the genuine care and love he has for animals.

He got our very sick cat back to full health and I'll forever be thankful to him.

It's hard to put into words what we experienced today. We came to Dublin from Cork to consult our cat with cardiologist Tom. The wonderful treatment we received, the empathetic, calm, yet matter-of-fact way Tom guided us through the scan, explained everything thoroughly, and answered every question, is simply impossible to describe in a single comment. I wish everyone good health, but if you ever need a specialist, I hope you meet someone like Tom. Thank you, Sonia & Lubo, and the wonderful Frida ❤️‍🩹🫀
P.S. The ladies at the front desk were also wonderful!

Excellent care , professionalism and warmth was shown to Travis , our cat , on his recent visit to Rebecca Rennick. All aspects of the procedure were of the highest standard and after care / advice was impeccable. I would highly recommend Rebecca and the team in  Nutgrove Vets.

My general opinion about this vet place is normal. There are normal doctors and nice pet care. BUT…

Just one issue we had today and I feel like I need to leave a review about it. Just about it.

Nail clip.
Guys, this is a disaster. We have been to many places but this was just not right, honestly. They tortured my dog. And told that it was my fault. My dog is not biting, very friendly. She may not let to take her feet. Trying to escape. But after what that woman did to her, my dog will never let it again at all. And will not trust to any nail clipper.
They returned my puppy to me and told: She is too nervous. You must give her sedative before bringing here.

Excuse me, but it is so unprofessional. In any other place it takes 3-5 mins to do it. Not 20. Without blood, hurting and drama. Professionals never hold pets with hands, like you do. Maybe for small breeds it works but not for medium or big size dogs. Looks like the only nervous person was that woman.

35 euro for this! If I knew, I would never let it happen. Would be nice to get a refund for this unprofessional thing.

So all I can do is just to recommend to go to a different place for this service.
Any other, examination or vaccination, maybe it is ok. But nail clipping just avoid if you love your dog.
Very good vetenarian advice.
You know your pet is in good hands and cared for in this vet practice
Your pet is in the best of care here, top notch vets with leading edge equipment. Very fortunate to have this practice in the locality.

Myself and my wife Elsie have been with this practice for the last 20 years or more.  During this time we have experienced only the best of care for our cats, and ourselves too.  Our current cat Pablo, is enjoying the the same quality of care with his current health problems. We found them very compassionate, kind and helpful when our cats needed end of live care. We have always found the receptionis and nurses very kind and helpful to us especially as we are in the winter of our lives. We would happily recommemd them to any person searching for a reliable, superbly qualified and personable Veterinary Practice
Kind and compassionate service.  Very thorough and considerate, especially when delivering sensitive news.

I can’t speak highly enough of this veterinary practice. Every single vet we have dealt with has provided outstanding care for my dog, Galileo. Most recently, Dr Tom Mullaney and Dr Rebecca Rennick expertly assisted Galileo with stomach issues. The diagnosis was efficient, thorough, and reassuring, and their care made a real difference to his recovery.

Over time, we have also been treated by Dr William Hayden, Dr Fiona Higgins, and Dr Dara O’Hanlon, and without exception they have all provided the same consistently excellent standard of care. Each visit leaves me feeling confident that Galileo is in the best possible hands, and he has come away better every single time.

The nursing staff and wider team are equally exceptional – warm, caring, patient, and genuinely compassionate. As a pet owner, that level of kindness and professionalism means everything. I couldn’t be happier with the service and care my dog has received here and would recommend this practice without hesitation.

Darragh really has let the team down with my most recent experience. My puppy Teddy was experiencing stomach issues, vomiting and diarrhoea. After taking his temperature (Teddy didn’t like this but Darragh was able to get a reading, I held Teddy in my arms and Darragh claimed Teddy went to bite him, this was not apparent from where I stood). Darragh asked if he could take Teddy upstairs so a nurse could hold him for an anal glands examination. He was gone for maybe 2 minutes, 30-50 seconds of which I could hear my puppy screaming…..
Darragh then enters the room with my puppy on a tightly constricted leash around his neck and throws the leash at me “this behaviour is completely unacceptable from a dog, I cannot examine him”.
Bearing in mind this was my second trip with my puppy, there was no issue when Fiona examined him a few months previous.
Darragh then said he’d have to guess at what it was, gastroenteritis and to “give it a few days”. Anyone who’s owned dogs for years could guess that, as I have.
Along with owning many pets over the years, I’ve dealt with many vets. Darragh has an appalling way of dealing with animals. It’s a shame as both Fiona and Rebecca have been amazing. Would not recommend Darragh and don’t think he should practice in consultations, stick to surgery where both human and animal don’t have to deal with his awful manner.
Very kind, helpful and went above & beyond, thanks!

Our dog was referred here to see a specialist cardiologist. We were very impressed by the level of care, attention and detail during the consulation and susbsequent scans.  Tom was excellent to deal with, explaining everything to us with great patience. Couldnt recommend more highly.

Put right at ease by all the staff and Tom. Best experience we've had at a veterinarians, our lil Pixie wasn't half as scared as she normally is. Super calming atmosphere and lovely waiting area. Staff are superb. Tom is an amazing Vetenarian - explained the cardiac scan in detail to help us understand exactly what was going on with our lil girl. Would highly recommend.

I feel compelled to write this as an act of justice for my beloved dog, Alfie, who had been a patient at Nutgrove for several years. Alfie was treated for hip dysplasia and received monthly medication administered by a nurse. From time to time, we saw Darragh Hanlon.

In recent months, Alfie began to suffer from nosebleeds. I brought him in to see Darragh, who prescribed antibiotics. However, when discussing what to do if they didn’t work, he told me—very bluntly—that there were only two options: euthanasia or a rhinoscopy. The way this was communicated was not just abrupt, but incredibly insensitive.

Darragh, from my past experiences, was never particularly warm, but I had believed he had Alfie’s best interests at heart. That belief changed after that visit. His manner was cold, dismissive, impatient and frankly, rude. It left me feeling hurt and alone at a time when I needed support and understanding.

Our next visit was with Rebecca, and the contrast couldn’t have been more stark. She showed kindness and empathy towards both Alfie and me. Her approach reminded me of what veterinary care should feel like—compassionate, attentive, and human.

More recently, I brought Alfie to Michael in Allcare, Walkinstown. From the moment we arrived, Michael showed genuine warmth and affection toward Alfie. Together, we discussed the heartbreaking decision to plan Alfie’s euthanasia. Michael sat down with me and walked me through the process with compassion, patience, and respect.

After 13 wonderful years with Alfie, this is the kind of care and understanding he deserved. I am so grateful to Michael for restoring my faith in what veterinary care can and should be. And I am deeply relieved that Alfie’s final moments will be surrounded by dignity and love.

Leaving Nutgrove was the right decision, and while I wish things had been different, I hope that by sharing this experience, it may encourage greater empathy, patience and sensitivity in future patient care.

My partner took our dog Rua to see Tom the other week, and he correctly diagnosed a hernia in our dog. Our family has had many years experience with this vet clinic and mainly deal with Tom and William.... They are the best and this is not like a business to them but they really love what they do. Tom like William are the best and take great care of your fur baby... Thank you so much for your professionalism and the time you take with our pets.
Amazing vets everyone so nice to deal with and really care about your animals. William in particular was the most amazing vet

Last year I brought my cat to Darragh O'Hanlon. He diagnosed conjunctivitis with eye drops as treatment. When after two weeks there was no improvement I brought the cat to Mark Heffernan on Whitehall Road and he immediately said the cat had Entropion where lower lids turn in on eye causing painful friction and ulceration if not corrected and ultimately blindness. Only an operation would correct. One eye that was shut closed was already ulcerated. He said it was a straightforward diagnosis. Mark did the operation the following morning, I had to keep the cat indoors and treat with tablets and drops for a month. Thankfully he made a full recovery.

My cat suffered intense pain for two more weeks than he needed to. There's a lot more to this sorry tale but the nub of it is as outlined. I found the attitude of this vet and his boss, Tom to be arrogant and unprofessional. They 'stood over' the diagnosis and treatment.

This place it’s the best. I am eternally grateful to doctor Tom Mullany, he saved my dog’s life, he’s a blessing to us and to medicine! My dog has a cardiac problem and thanks to Tom my dog still with us.

Best place you can go without a doubt.
Lovely vets very professional

I have to say, today, I experienced one of the most professional veterinary consults ever. My dachshund Frankie was in to see Darragh for review of a dermatology issue. Darragh was extremely professional, meticulous, considerate and expert in his diagnosis. He took the time to explain and work through the issue, even whiteboarding it to explain it clearer. I am extremely impressed and feel confident that Frankie is in good hands. We'll done, superb service.

I've brought my Golden Retriever here for years and found the practice very accommodating to get him booked in when I need it. Bilbo's vet William Hayden is always very patient and answers any queries I have and never rushes our appointment, he was also very compassionate when we had a cancer scare with our dog a year ago and quickly arranged for a surgery in house that successfully removed the tumor. I've had a very pleasant experience with anyone I've encountered at the clinic. Bilbo is always a very happy dog entering and leaving the clinic.

It was my pet's first visit, and I was very happy with the service everyone was very helpful and super professional, I recommend .

I absolutely love this clinic for bringing my dog to. She sees Dr Tom Mullany annually for a cardiology appointment and he treats her as if she is own pet with utmost care and respect. He is so gentle to Dolly and always talks me through …

Really wonderful veterinary practice, the vets and nurses are clearly passionate about animals and can't do enough for you. We've been bringing our two dogs for 6 or 7 years now and wouldn't use any other practice, they look after us so …
